overall_summary: Data shows a strong shift toward 'self respect' concepts featuring actionable digital boundaries (e.g., chat deletion, hiding blue ticks, muted chats), yielding 30-40 views consistently compared to passive emotional topics (5-17 views). Confidence remains moderate due to low overall view counts.

winning_patterns.pattern: Self-respect tied to digital boundaries (chat actions, blue ticks, status hidden)
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on self respect averaged 29 views, with peak performance at 40 views (AfaLxMy6FMY - chat delete) and 39 views (rwOUYo_hayQ - status list).
winning_patterns.action: Double down on micro-actions people take on smartphones to enforce personal boundaries.

weak_patterns.pattern: Passive night thoughts / Overthinking without an active turning point
weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'रात के ख्याल' and 'ओवरथिंकिंग' logged lowest views (5 to 17 views).
weak_patterns.action: Avoid purely passive sadness; always ground the narrative in a decisive moment of moving on.

next_video.concept: Removing someone's media auto-download setting to stop saving memories automatically.
next_video.opening_direction: Show fingers turning off 'Media Auto-Download' specifically for one pinned chat.
next_video.twist_direction: The realization that deleting photos isn't enough; stopping new memories from taking space in your gallery is where peace begins.
next_video.reason: Top-performing videos consistently utilize phone settings/ui actions as emotional visual metaphors during the 13:40 UTC posting window.

experiment: Testing if setting-specific UI actions (Media Auto-Download) drive stronger relatable resonance than chat/status deletion.
